name: Harold Holt
bio: One of the young men of George Ives's household; Cook identifies him as Ives's grandmother's former secretary, named alongside James Goddard as sharing Ives's rooms at E4 the Albany - and sometimes his bed - from 1894.
bio_sources: Cook, London and the Culture of Homosexuality (2003), pp. 146, 148
bio_note: Cook 2003, p. 146 names the two men sharing Ives's bed as 'James Goddard (Kit)' and 'Harold Holt (Cubby)'; Cook 2014, p. 101 instead identifies the long-term resident nicknamed Cubby as 'Charles Gee', and the name Holt does not appear in the 2014 book at all - so the only source for him remains Cook 2003 p. 146, which names him but gives no dates. Cook is the only scholar to have written this household up, and he dates arrivals, departures and Ives's will but never a person: no birth or death date is given for any member of the household. Ives's own proved will (Cook, printed pp. 109-110), which leaves the Adelaide Road house to Bloodworth and Saunders, names Bloodworth an executor and portions the Goddards, is the natural documentary starting point.
